# Results -- Study 527 (Organizational-Capital) on the real EDGAR + yfinance tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Protocol: capitalize SG&A by
perpetual inventory (Eisfeldt-Papanikolaou 2013; depreciation `delta = 0.15`, steady-state
seed), scale by total assets, sort the basket annually, go long the high-OC half / short the
low-OC half with one execution lag, measure the monthly spread with a Newey-West HAC *t*.
As-of **2026-06-26**.*

## Data stamp

| Frame | Shape | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|
| Fundamentals (annual SG&A + total assets, EDGAR 10-K) | 643 firm-years × 38 firms | `0acb116f3220` |
| Prices (daily adjusted-close, yfinance) | 4275 days × 39 tickers | `26dc45209cc1` |
| Fund years covered | 2007 -- 2026 | -- |
| Price period covered | 2009-01-02 -- 2025-12-30 | -- |

**Source:** SG&A and total assets from **EDGAR** (data.sec.gov XBRL company-facts, 10-K
annual frames; where a firm reports SG&A split into Selling&Marketing + G&A we sum them).
Prices from yfinance daily adjusted-close (auto_adjust=True). Basket: ~40 large-cap names
spanning consumer staples, retail, tech, telecom and industrials -- chosen for real SG&A
dispersion. 38 firms cleared the EDGAR pull; 39 cleared the price pull (the long-short uses
their intersection per year).

**Survivorship bias (named explicitly):** the basket is current large-caps that still trade
in 2026. Firms that went bankrupt or were acquired -- the high-risk tail an organizational-
capital *risk* story would load onto the long leg -- are absent. Any positive result would be
an **upper bound**. Here the result is negative regardless.

**Data limitation:** EDGAR gives ~18-19 years of SG&A per large-cap (vs the multi-decade,
delisted-inclusive Compustat panel of the original paper). The perpetual inventory is seeded
at steady state, so the early-year stock carries seed assumptions; the *cross-sectional rank*
is robust to this (and to the depreciation rate -- see robustness).

## The honest test -- high-minus-low org-capital long-short

Each year, the basket is split at the median of `oc/assets`; the long leg is the high-OC half,
the short leg the low-OC half, equal-weighted, held 12 months, entered one period after the
signal is public.

| Statistic | Value |
|---|---|
| N months | 203 (2009-02 -- 2025-12) |
| Basket (priced) | 39 names |
| Mean long-short (annualised) | **-1.68%/yr** *(gross)* |
| Vol (annualised) | 7.60%/yr |
| Sharpe (annual) | -0.221 |
| **HAC t-stat** | **-0.923** |
| Hit rate (months > 0) | 52.2% |
| Max drawdown | -31.4% |

- The high-minus-low spread earns **-1.68%/yr** at HAC *t* = **-0.923** -- below the
  |*t*| >= 2 bar **and with the wrong sign**. Eisfeldt-Papanikolaou (2013) predict a *positive*
  premium; on this survivor basket the high-OC half *under*performs.
- **High-OC leg: +14.96%/yr. Low-OC leg: +16.65%/yr.** The leg that should win loses by ~1.7%/yr.

## Net of costs

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Transaction cost | 5 bps/leg one-way, charged at the annual rebalance (100% turnover assumed) |
| Short borrow | 50 bps/yr on the short leg, charged monthly |
| **Net long-short (annualised)** | **-2.28%/yr** |
| Net HAC t-stat | -1.248 |

The gross spread is already negative; costs only deepen the loss. There is nothing to trade.

## Placebo -- shuffle the org-capital labels within each year

| Statistic | Value |
|---|---|
| Real long-short mean | -0.1403%/mo |
| Null mean (shuffled labels) | +0.0127%/mo (std 0.1373%) |
| **Placebo p-value** | **0.326** (500 shuffles) |

The real long-short sits comfortably inside the label-shuffled null distribution. We cannot
reject the hypothesis that the org-capital ranking carries no information about returns on this
basket.

## Robustness -- depreciation rate

| `delta` | Long-short | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| 0.10 | -1.71%/yr | -0.920 |
| 0.15 | -1.68%/yr | -0.923 |
| 0.20 | -2.06%/yr | -1.130 |
| 0.30 | -1.93%/yr | -1.051 |

Negative and insignificant across every plausible depreciation rate -- the verdict does not
hinge on the perpetual-inventory parameter.

## Synthetic positive control (engine power check ONLY -- never cited for the real verdict)

The full pipeline is run on a synthetic world with a *planted* OC premium, averaging the
long-short HAC *t* over 12 RNG seeds (so no single lucky seed can pose as signal):

| Planted premium | Long-short (%/yr) | Mean HAC *t* (12 seeds) |
|---|--:|--:|
| -0.06 | -10.17% | -4.41 |
| -0.03 | -5.38% | -2.36 |
| 0.00 | -0.60% | -0.27 |
| +0.03 | +4.19% | +1.83 |
| +0.06 | +8.98% | +3.92 |
| +0.10 | +15.36% | +6.62 |

The long-short is monotone in the planted premium and **correctly signed** (positive premium
-> positive, significant long-short; zero -> noise). The engine is faithful: the wrong-signed,
insignificant result on the real tape is **the market**, not the method.

## Verdict

- **Signal -- NONE.** -1.68%/yr, HAC *t* = -0.923, the *wrong sign*, placebo *p* = 0.326,
  negative across every depreciation rate. No literature upgrade: the published premium lives
  on a broad, delisted-inclusive Compustat universe we cannot reproduce on a survivor basket,
  and here the *sign itself* fails. This is None, not Weak.
- **Tradability -- MIRAGE.** Net -2.28%/yr, Sharpe -0.221, max drawdown -31.4%. The gross
  spread is negative; costs make it worse. Nothing to trade.
- **Premium-sign -- BUSTED.** Eisfeldt-Papanikolaou predict high-OC > low-OC by ~4.6%/yr; on
  this basket the sign flips. The synthetic control proves the engine recovers a correctly-
  signed planted premium, so the flip is the tape (and the survivor truncation of the high-risk
  long leg), not a bug.
